acks.detail: fleet/race-launch.mjs — a real race: K live drives of one plan (VM provisioning, branch push, PR creation) launched by `node fleet/race.mjs launch <plan> <raceId>` — Every test injects `driveOne`, the git runner, `readToken` and `exec`; the real path needs the orchestrator, sandbox VMs, a GitHub remote and an OAuth token, none of which exist here. Concurrency, manifest-before-drive ordering and allSettled behaviour are proven against stubs only. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

fleet/race-clone.mjs — that a per-run clone with `remote set-url origin <https>` is genuinely publishable (the defect the task exists to prevent) — The tests assert the recorded argv sequence against a stub; no git remote or network is available, so only the shape of the fix is verified, not that the resulting clone can push. The single live subprocess is `gitRunner(['--version'])` (test:149), which the green suite did execute. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

fleet/race-judge.mjs:40 `defaultExec` — the real `execFile('sqlite3', <dbDir>/fleet.db, 'SELECT store FROM tinybase LIMIT 1')` store read — No sqlite3 binary in this environment, and `readStore` is injected in every judge test, so the default exec path is never entered. The argv literal is pinned by test_race_evidence.mjs:136 and matches status.mjs:79's own literal, but the actual sqlite invocation and its `code`/`stdout` contract are unexecuted. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

fleet/race-manifest.mjs DIALS — the `winnerDefectSurface` dial ("the winner's post-merge defect surface, anything traced back within the next two sittings") — A pre-registered measurement dial whose value can only be filled in by an operator observing the two sittings after a merge; nothing in the tree can evaluate it.
